header.running_head: Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Distribute Everything in the Baytul Maal

blocks.text: Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA) Distribute Everything in the Baytul Maal
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Distributes all the wealth and Rejects the Proposal of a person who Advocated Keeping Reserves

Hadhrat Sa'eed narrates that Hadhrat Umar (RA) instructed (the public treasurer) Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Arqam (RA) to distribute everything in the Baytul Maal every month. Thereafter, he issued instructions for everything to be distributed once a week. He eventually gave the instruction for the distribution to be on a daily basis. Someone then said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Why do you not keep something in reserve for an emergency or when other areas call for assistance?" Addressing the person, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "It is Shaytaan speaking on your lips. Allaah has inspired me with the answer and protected me from the evil of the act. What I have prepared for such situations is exactly what Rasulullaah ﷺ had prepared, and that is obedience to Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ."[^1]
The Narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) reports that some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA) from Iraq. He was about to distribute it when someone stood up to say, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! Why do you rather not reserve this wealth to fend off an enemy that may suddenly attack or for another unforeseen emergency that may strike?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) admonished the person saying, "What is the mater with you?! May you be destroyed! It is Shaytaan speaking with your tongue. Allaah has inspired me with the response and I swear by Allaah that I shall never disobey Him today for the emergencies of tomorrow. I shall not (do as you say) but shall rather prepare for the Muslims that which Rasulullaah ﷺ had prepared for them (obedience to Allaah and Rasulullaah ﷺ)."[^2]
The Incident Between Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA)

Hadhrat Salamah bin Sa'eed reports that when some wealth once came to Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) approached him saying, "Why do you rather not keep this money in reserve in the Baytul Maal for any emergency that may arise or for anything else that may occur?"
